title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: Writing blocks edit drafts, memos and emails inline
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap's planned inline editing capability and its overdue target without treating it as launched. The documented app-blocking path is correct, the conflicting Microsoft descriptions of its reach are reported, and targeted searches found no Writing blocks-specific controls or licensing details.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Writing blocks as inline editing and iteration on drafts, memos, emails and other writing while using Chat.
claims.quote: M365 Copilot now supports Writing blocks. Edit drafts, memos, emails, and more inline while using Chat for easy editing and iteration.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe Writing blocks.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Writing blocks" Copilot' and '"Writing blocks" Copilot Chat default admin settings license meter storage identity'; opened Copilot overview, Manage Copilot Chat and release notes; searched fetched release notes for 'writing block' with no matches.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Writing blocks' arrival default is unknown, and no source states that existing Chat behaviour changes automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot "Writing blocks" license pricing credits limits default'; opened Manage Copilot Chat, Copilot overview and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; the roadmap and these pages state no Writing blocks default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No Writing blocks-specific tenant switch is documented in an admin UI or automation reference.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Writing blocks" "settings"' and '"Writing blocks" admin switch Graph PowerShell licensing storage'; opened Manage Copilot Chat and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; neither documents a Writing blocks switch.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Learn documents no API equivalent for blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph PowerShell block Copilot app Integrated Apps API availability users' and '"Integrated Apps" "block" "API" Copilot'; opened Integrated Apps and copilotPackage: block. The latter blocks catalog packages, not the Copilot app.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The app-blocking path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. ... Select Block app.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope
claims.claim: The cited Integrated Apps page says its controls are available only to Global Admins.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Blocking the Copilot app blocks Chat access more broadly than a Writing blocks-only switch.
claims.quote: Users blocked through Integrated Apps see the Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization experience when opening Copilot Chat in the Copilot app.

claims.where: Governance controls

claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat says this setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and Chat on the web.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The general Integrated Apps page instead says app blocking affects only the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook.

claims.where: Governance controls

claims.quote: Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center and for Outlook apps made in the Exchange admin center.
